text:
maria: FYI saw repeated OOMs on pt-serve-25 during the nightly kv-cache replay after yesterday's kernel-routing change. happened ~03:20 UTC, multiple shards.
jonathan: ugh. any logs? stack traces?
maria: pasted the tail, looks like allocation failures when cudaMalloc tries to split a large slab.
```
E CudaOutOfMemoryError: cannot allocate 1.40 GiB (GPU 0; 47.66 GiB total capacity; 43.20 GiB already allocated)
  File "/app/runtime/allocator.py", line 412, in allocate
    ptr = cuda_malloc(size)
```
liz: what were the allocator knobs set to? expandable_segments? max_split_size_mb? gc threshold?
maria: current config on that pool: `{
  "expandable_segments": "on",
  "max_split_size_mb": "64",
  "garbage_collection_threshold": "0.25"
}`
sam: kv-cache warmup + long min-seq kernels increase fragmentation. when max_split_size_mb is small, allocator does many splits and tiny free lists proliferate.
ryan: thinking out loud: either raise `max_split_size_mb` to avoid excessive splitting or tune GC to be more aggressive so we coalesce earlier.
jonathan: can we reproduce with a short script that simulates many prefix writes and a kernel routing change triggering bigger tiled kernels?
maria: yes i made a repro harness that replays fetches at 2048 token context with 8 concurrent streams. landed in /infra/projs/kv-repro.
liz: ran quick matrix last night. summary:
```
config                         | OOMs | median latency | tail alloc frag
max_split_size_mb=64,gc=0.25   | 4    | 72ms           | high
max_split_size_mb=128,gc=0.25  | 1    | 76ms           | medium
max_split_size_mb=256,gc=0.25  | 0    | 82ms           | low
max_split_size_mb=128,gc=0.4   | 0    | 79ms           | low
```
sam: interesting — bigger splits reduced OOMs but added a bit of latency on median (kernel choice maybe selecting larger attention kernels).
jonathan: do we care about that +10ms if it prevents OOMs? for high-SLO customers maybe no, but default for hosted should prefer stability.
maria: also saw that expandable_segments=on sometimes delays reclaim until segment grows; with high concurrency that increases peak reserved. tried `expandable_segments=off` and observed slightly fewer peaks but more GC churn.
ryan: propose an intermediate: enable expandable but tweak `garbage_collection_threshold` upward and add opportunistic compaction during idle periods. e.g. set gc threshold=0.35 and schedule a compaction pass after heavy KV warmups.
liz: added a small compaction hook in runtime: `if kv_warmup_complete and idle_for_ms > 200: compact_fragments()` — tested on canary and recycled ~3.1 GiB of fragmented memory.
deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime/canary/kv-compaction-heuristic v2026.03.18-rc1
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded to canary (6 instances)
jonathan: can we enable per-pool overrides so dedicated pools for high-throughput customers use max_split_size_mb=256 while default stays 128?
maria: yes config supports per-pool. I pushed a per-pool override for `pt-serve-25` to 256 and GC to 0.35.
sam: ran longer soak (6h) with 64 concurrent streams and no OOMs so far. tail latency steady.
liz: left a profiling snapshot: `/snapshots/2026-03-18/pt-serve-25/kv-warmup-compact.json` showing a 19% drop in fragmentation index after compaction pass.
ryan: next steps: 1) roll compaction to more canaries 2) add a metrics gauge for fragmentation by pool 3) add autosuggest in Optimize to recommend `max_split_size_mb` based on observed split rate.
jonathan: also add a regression test in CI that fuzzes allocator knobs across kernel routing matrix to catch perf regressions early.
maria: creating issue and PRs. i'll coordinate with infra to run broader perf matrix.
sam: thanks team, great iterative triage. :thumbsup:
